source_document: Document 13 — How a Law Gets Built (Unit 1 Casefile B)
source_text: 1705 — Virginia slave codes: all Black, mulatto and Indian enslaved people are declared real property — legally real estate. Forbidden to assault a white person, denied the right to bear arms, denied movement without written permission.
prompt: Write 2-3 sentences of historical context for this law.
checklist: Did you name the era or decades this fits in?
Did you name what was happening in Virginia during this period?
Did you connect it to why this law mattered?
model_response: By the early 1700s, Virginia's laws had spent decades separating enslaved people from indentured servants, stripping away rights one at a time. The 1705 slave codes finished that process by declaring enslaved people to be real property, not people — which is why this document matters: it shows slavery becoming permanent under the law, not just in practice.
